The new Result-status row (e29688bb0, mirrored by 3f2c78673 into content/plugin-docs/services.json) claims 'The service rows that were decoded are still emitted' for services:malformed_launchctl_capture. plugin-developer traced the code and found this FALSE, not merely vacuously true: services_parsers.hpp's parse_launchctl_list returns immediately on raw.malformed, BEFORE the row-decode loop runs -- zero rows are ever decoded, not just zero rows surviving a filter. enumerate_services_macos's services vector and do_list's write-output loop are consequently empty every time this status fires -- zero svc| rows are ever emitted, with no exception. The sentence reads, by direct analogy to the services:output_truncated row immediately above it (which genuinely does emit partial rows before its byte-cap cutoff), as a claim that this status also ships partial data -- it never does. docs-writer independently reached the same wording-level conclusion in a parallel sub-review. plugin-developer's proposed correction: 'No service rows are ever emitted for this status -- the malformed check fires before any row decoding is attempted, so the caller gets a clean svc| row count of zero -- but the result is never reported as a clean, complete listing; before this, a truncated capture read as a genuine "0 services" success.' Non-blocking (no security bypass, no data loss, runtime behavior is safe and self-consistent -- only the doc's description of it is wrong); requires a follow-up wording fix to the README row (and a mirroring plugin_doc_gen.py --all regeneration) before this table entry can be trusted as accurate integrator-facing documentation.
